spec.mathematics: Strip width 8 cm; successive heights from top are 5, 3, 5 and 3 cm. Side flaps are 5 by 3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Face labels and measurements are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
Front and back: $(5\times8)\times2=80\text{ cm}^{2}$.

Sides: $(3\times5)\times2=30\text{ cm}^{2}$.

Bottom and top: $(3\times8)\times2=48\text{ cm}^{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=80+30+48\\&=158\text{ cm}^{2}.\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Using the face orientation of the solid:

Front and back: $(3\times2)\times2=12\text{ cm}^{2}$.

Sides: $(5\times2)\times2=20\text{ cm}^{2}$.

Bottom and top: $(3\times5)\times2=30\text{ cm}^{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=12+20+30\\&=62\text{ cm}^{2}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rectangular prism with two single equality ticks on the front lower edge and lower right receding edge. No height label or height equality tick is supplied. Ordinary source blue and red strokes become black; hidden edges remain dashed.
spec.mathematics: Two adjacent base edges are equal and measure 8.2 m. The height is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and equality marks are visible.

answer.short: Insufficient information: the height is missing.
answer.worked:
The equality marks give a square base of side $8.2\,\mathrm{m}$, but do not establish the height. If the height is $h$ metres, the face-pair method gives
$$\begin{aligned}A&=2(8.2\times8.2)+2(8.2h)+2(8.2h)\\A&=134.48+32.8h\quad\mathrm{m}^2.\end{aligned}$$
A numerical surface area requires the height. If the intended solid is a cube, its surface area is $403.44\,\mathrm{m}^2$.

spec.description: Tall rectangular prism with depth receding towards the upper left, labelled 1 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm. Source decorative edge colours are replaced by black, retaining hidden-edge dashes.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular prism dimensions 1 cm by 2 cm by 3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions only; no answer appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Front and back: $(1\times3)\times2=6\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.

Sides: $(2\times3)\times2=12\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.

answer.short: The triangular prism tent has $7.6\text{ m}^2$ more surface area.
answer.worked:
Triangular prism tent, including the floor:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangular}}&=2\left(\frac12\times2\times2\right)+2(2.24\times5)+2\times5\\A_{\text{triangular}}&=4+22.4+10\\A_{\text{triangular}}&=36.4\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
Half-cylinder tent, including both ends and the floor, with $r=1\text{ m}$:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{half-cylinder}}&=2\left(\frac12\pi(1)^2\right)+\frac12\times2\pi(1)(5)+2\times5\\A_{\text{half-cylinder}}&=\pi+5\pi+10\\A_{\text{half-cylinder}}&=(10+6\pi)\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Difference}&=36.4-(10+6\pi)\\\text{Difference}&\approx7.6\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
The triangular prism tent has the greater surface area.

content.prompt: A log with diameter 60 cm is 3 m in length. Its hollow centre is 20 cm in diameter. Find the surface area of the log in cm², including the ends and the inside, correct to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Hollow cylindrical log extending towards the upper right, with annular front end, outer silhouettes, concealed inner surface and rear-end geometry. Both diameter dimension cues are retained; ordinary visible and dashed edges use black.
spec.mathematics: Outer diameter 60 cm, inner diameter 20 cm and length 3 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; supplied working is stored in the answer.

answer.worked:
$3\text{ m}=300\text{ cm}$.

Circular ends:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{ends}}&=\bigl[\pi(30^2)-\pi(10^2)\bigr]\times2\\&=1600\pi\end{aligned}$$
Outside:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{outside}}&=2\pi(30)(300)\\&=18\,000\pi\end{aligned}$$
Inside:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{inside}}&=2\pi(10)(300)\\&=6000\pi\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{total}}&=1600\pi+18\,000\pi+6000\pi\\&=25\,600\pi\\&\approx80\,424.8\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

entries.description:
Supplied blue working, in source order:
Dimensions of can: r = 37 mm, h = 222 mm
Circular ends = 2π(37)² = 2738π mm²
Curved surface = 2π(37)(222) = 16428π mm²
Cans needed = 48000 ÷ 3 = 16 000
Strong aluminium needed = 2738π × 16000 = 43 808 000π mm² ÷ 1000² = 43.808π m²
Thin aluminium needed = 16428π × 16000 = 262 848 000π mm² ÷ 1000² = 262.848π m²
Cost of thin aluminium = 43.808π × $5.60 = $770.7105894 …
Cost of strong aluminium = 262.848π × $4.80 = $3963.65446 …
Total cost = $4734.37
